title: Carnevale–Voll's unitary-factor conjecture for Euler–Mahonian distributions
statement:
Let $\rho$ be a composition of $N$, and let $R\subseteq [N-1]$ be constructed from $\rho$ as in the source. Write

$$
C_\rho(x,q)=\sum_{w\in S_N^{R^c}}x^{\operatorname{stc}(w)}q^{\ell(w)}.
$$

A **unitary factor** means a nonconstant factor of the form $1+xq^a$.

**Carnevale–Voll's conjecture.** The polynomial $C_\rho(x,q)$ has a unitary factor if and only if $\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_m)$ has all parts equal to some odd integer $r$ and $m$ is even. In that case,

$$
C_\rho(x,q)=(1+xq^{\frac{rm}{2}})\widetilde{C}_\rho(x,q),
$$

for some $\widetilde{C}_\rho(x,q)\in\mathbb{Z}[x,q]$ with no unitary factors.

This conjecture characterizes exactly when the bivariate Euler–Mahonian distribution on the relevant symmetric-group quotient has a unitary factor, and specifies that factor and its exponent.
source_name: Angela Carnevale, “On some Euler-Mahonian distributions”, arXiv:1612.00426 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.00426

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).
